title: Golden Horde
capsule: The Golden Horde (Mongolian/Turkic: Uluğ Ulus, 'Great State') was the northwestern ulus of the Mongol Empire, founded by Batu Khan after the westward campaigns of 1236–1242 and formalized as an independent polity under Möngke Temür in the 1260s. At its height under Öz Beg Khan (r. 1313–1341), it controlled the Pontic-Caspian steppe from the Danube to the Irtysh and extracted tribute from the Rus' principalities. A catastrophic defeat by Timur at the Battle of the Vorskla River (1399) and Timur's sack of Sarai (1395) shattered its power; it fragmented into the Kazan, Astrakhan, Crimean, and other successor khanates through the fifteenth century, with the Great Horde (its last remnant) dissolved by the Crimean Khanate in 1502.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core steppe territory is reasonably well attested; frontier zones in Rus', the Caucasus, and Central Asia shifted frequently and are reconstructed largely from chronicle evidence and numismatic finds.
